findings.reason: Clarified that charge labels, including inputs and total charge, are chosen representatives in Irr(C), resolving the zero- and one-input identity cases. This matches Penneys' representative convention ([Definition 3.5.1](https://people.math.osu.edu/penneys.2/UQSL/ArchivedNotes/TPM/FusionCats.pdf)).
The proof now chooses orthogonal semisimple decompositions before using their inclusions and projections, and states the representative-label convention in its count.
The multiplicity-space basis is now the adjoint projection a⊗b→c; the inclusion c→a⊗b remains in the coevaluation construction.

Corrected the claim that ordinary finite-dimensional vector spaces are strict monoidal and no longer identifies their tensor powers literally with C. The scalar Yang–Baxter computation is made in the strictification.
Added Mac Lane coherence as an explicit supplier and included intervening tensor factors in the distant-commutativity proof.

The item claims an idempotent for any fusion category but uses QC25 F/tree interfaces scoped to unitary fusion categories. The owner must add a general F-coordinate supplier or reconcile the domain; thm-anyonic-channel-projectors-are-reparenthesization-independent has the same generality mismatch.

The fixed total c is not explicitly required to be a simple representative, while the linked fusion-tree and F/R interfaces are defined for simple total labels. The linked theorem thm-qc-tqc-braid-action-unitary-and-artin repeats this omission. The owner should state c∈Irr(C) or supply a nonsimple-total extension.
The item uses V(x^n→c) with the QC25 unitary tree inner product without stating the category and simple representative charge domain. The owner should make that domain explicit.

The task fixes simple charge labels but does not explicitly require its total charge to be one of those simple representatives. def-qa-37-fusion-input-encoding inherits this domain and needs owner reconciliation.
